stem: A manufacturer publishes EquipmentInspectionCompleted events on an EventBridge bus in account A. Independent maintenance and warranty systems in accounts B and C each need a copy, filtered by inspection type. The current design forwards A events to B, where a rule attempts to forward the received events to C. B receives events, but C does not. All accounts are in the same Region, and downstream processing already handles duplicate deliveries. The company wants managed routing without a custom republishing service. Which TWO changes should the architect make? (Select TWO.)
options: Add another forwarding rule in B with a higher-priority event pattern and keep the A-to-B-to-C topology.
Configure rules on A to target the required destination buses in B and C directly.
Configure receiving bus resource policies and sending target roles for the authorized cross-account deliveries; filter the source account and inspection types in destination rules.
Enable an EventBridge archive in B and rely on the archive to propagate every newly received event to C.
Move C to a different Region so B can forward the unchanged cross-account event onward.

stem: A shipping company uses a workflow to validate a hazardous-goods declaration, obtain approval from an external inspection portal, and book transport. Approval can take up to 48 hours. The portal can call an authenticated application endpoint when the decision is made. Which architecture meets these requirements?
options: Use an Express Workflow with a task token and keep its execution waiting until the portal returns the token.
Run a Lambda function that submits the approval request and sleeps until the portal records a decision.

Use a Standard Workflow callback task. Securely retain its token in the backend, submit the portal request, and have the authorized backend return task success or failure after validating the portal decision.
Use a Standard Workflow request-response task that submits the portal request, then immediately execute the transport-booking state.

B: A long-running sleeping invocation is not the required durable wait and cannot accommodate the stated duration. C: A Standard callback task persists the wait without holding compute open. D: A successful submission response only acknowledges the request; it does not represent the later inspection approval.

stem: A consulting firm has a Bedrock Knowledge Base containing documents for many client engagements. Every ingested chunk has a trusted engagementId metadata value, and the selected vector store supports filtering that attribute. Consultants can work on several engagements but choose one authorized engagement for each chat. Only the application backend can call retrieval APIs. The firm must prevent content from other engagements from entering the model context, even when a user changes the question or requests another engagement ID. Which design best meets the requirement?
options: Retrieve across the entire knowledge base and instruct the model to hide unauthorized passages in its answer.
Have the browser provide a metadata filter and pass it unchanged to retrieval because the user has already signed in.

Resolve the selected engagement against server-side entitlements, reject unauthorized selections, and construct a mandatory engagementId retrieval filter on the backend before sending retrieved content to the model.
Remove citations from generated answers so users cannot discover the names of other engagement documents.

stem: A platform team creates VPCs for 60 AWS accounts in three Regions. Spreadsheets have led to accidental CIDR overlaps that block planned connectivity. stem: An image-processing role and its Amazon S3 bucket are in the same AWS account. A legacy bucket policy grants read access to one named assumed-role session of the processing role, and CloudTrail shows that session read an object under the restricted prefix. Which TWO statements identify the cause and a valid control? (Select TWO.)
options: The permissions boundary explicitly denies every action it does not list. Therefore the read could have occurred only because the bucket and the role are in different accounts.
A resource policy can grant access directly to a same-account assumed-role session. An implicit denial in the role's permissions boundary does not limit that direct grant.
Add a narrowing session policy with no Allow for the restricted prefix. An implicit denial there overrides any bucket-policy Allow to the named session.
Add an explicit s3:GetObject Deny for the restricted prefix to the centrally controlled permissions boundary on the processing role. Keep the existing allowance for public assets.
